learning_objective: 🌐 Master the Earth's imaginary grid! Learn how to find exact coordinates and calculate time zones across the world.

key_vocabulary.hindi_meaning: अक्षांश (भूमध्य रेखा के उत्तर या दक्षिण की कोणीय दूरी)
देशांतर (प्राइम मेरिडियन के पूर्व या पश्चिम की कोणीय दूरी)
भूमध्य रेखा / विषुवत रेखा (0° अक्षांश जो पृथ्वी को दो बराबर भागों में बांटती है)
प्रधान याम्योत्तर (0° देशांतर, जो ग्रीनविच से गुजरती है)
मानक समय (किसी देश के मध्य देशांतर का समय जो पूरे देश में माना जाता है)

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Imaginary lines running horizontally (East-West) around the Earth. The Equator is 0°. The North Pole is 90°N. Latitudes are parallel to each other and decrease in length as you move toward the poles.

Imaginary lines running vertically from the North Pole to the South Pole. The Prime Meridian (Greenwich, UK) is 0°. They are not parallel; they are furthest apart at the Equator and converge to a single point at the poles.

The intersecting network of latitudes and longitudes creates a grid called the graticule. With just two numbers (e.g., 28°N, 77°E), you can locate the exact position of any place on Earth (like New Delhi).

The Earth rotates 360° in 24 hours. That means it rotates 15° every hour, or 1° every 4 minutes. As the Earth rotates from West to East, places East of Greenwich are ahead in time, and places West are behind. (Rule: East Gain Add, West Lose Subtract - E.G.A., W.L.S.).

Local time is based on the overhead sun and changes every degree. To avoid chaos with train schedules and business, a country selects a central meridian (like 82°30'E for India) and its local time becomes the Standard Time for the whole country.

fun_activity.title: ⏳ Time Travel at the IDL
fun_activity.instructions: The International Date Line (IDL) roughly follows the 180° longitude in the Pacific Ocean. If you are standing on a ship and cross it going West, you instantly jump to 'tomorrow'. If you cross it going East, you travel back in time to 'yesterday'!

exam_tips: 📌 For time calculations, always remember: 1° of longitude = 4 minutes. Multiply the difference in longitude by 4 to get the time difference in minutes.
📌 Indian Standard Time (IST) is based on the 82°30'E longitude. Because it is East of Greenwich, India is exactly 5 hours and 30 minutes AHEAD of GMT (Greenwich Mean Time).
📌 The distance between two longitudes is maximum at the equator (~111 km) and strictly zero at the poles.
quick_recap: ⭐ The Equator is the largest possible circle that can be drawn on the globe (a Great Circle).
⭐ There are 181 parallels of latitude (90 N + 90 S + 1 Equator), but the poles are just points, not lines.
⭐ Some large countries like Russia, the USA, and Canada span so many longitudes that they use multiple time zones instead of just one.
